description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, b2-15).  Probe vs perl 5.40.3: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/misc1.pl row 4.  The idiom: generic dispatch code `if (blessed($x) && $x->isa("Regexp"))` / `ref($x) eq "Regexp"` (the second spelling works) / `$x->can(...)` on an arbitrary value / `re::is_regexp($x)` (probe it too).  perl: qr objects are blessed into package Regexp, so `->isa`, `->can`, `->DOES` and UNIVERSAL methods work, user code may even add methods to `Regexp::`, and `bless qr/x/, "My::Re"` re-blesses while STAYING a regex (probe: `"ax" =~ (bless qr/x/, "Foo")`).  Also: the die is a raw CL `error` with a BACKTRACE, not a perl die -- "Can't call method "isa" on unblessed reference" must be a trappable p-die (check the sibling raw `(error ...)` in p-method-call).  Low priority; runtime-only; full sweep + companion re/qr.t op/universal.t legs.


=== DONE (s495f, 2026-09-25) ===
Runtime only (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp):
  * %pcl-invocant-class's two fallback arms now ask %p-value-invocant-class: the handle class (#1074, unchanged) OR "Regexp" for a qr// payload with no class of its own -- so ->isa / ->can / ->DOES, UNIVERSAL methods and user subs in Regexp:: dispatch on a qr.  Reached only after the own-class and class-name-string readings miss: a blessed-object call never pays for it.
  * builtin::blessed (= Scalar::Util::blessed) no longer lists "Regexp" among the reftypes: blessed(qr/x/) is "Regexp" as in perl.
  * a blessed qr stringifies as its PATTERN (`bless qr/b+/, "Foo"` prints (?^:b+), was Foo=(?^:b+) -- pre-existing, same family); overload::StrVal of a qr is CLASS=REGEXP(0x..) (was SCALAR(0x1)).
  * re::is_regexp and re::regexp_pattern (core, universal.c -- callable without `use re`) defined in the RE package the pragma loop already makes; regexp_pattern's two list halves are cut from the ONE stringification.  Data::Dumper now prints qr/ab+c/i and bless( qr/y/, 'Foo' ) exactly as perl (it DIED "Can't handle 'Regexp' type" on base).
  * p-method-call's three raw CL `error`s ("Can't call method X on unblessed reference / an undefined value / non-blessed reference") are p-die now: trappable as before, and an uncaught one is one tidy line instead of an SBCL backtrace (perl's quoted "X" spelling).
Probes: scratch/s495f/p-qr.pl (11 lines), p-qr3.pl (Dumper, can-TO_JSON over 5 value kinds, a hash blessed INTO Regexp, map of qr, undef/class-string invocants), p-qr4.pl (regexp_pattern flags incl. a `:` in the pattern) -- identical to perl except qr//n (ruled, not-supported.md "Regex /n") and task #2340 (overloaded-"" qr as a pattern, pre-existing, filed).  ref(qr//) and plain stringification unchanged; interpolation of a qr into another pattern unchanged.
Bench control (quiet box, load ~1, BENCH_K=3; tree vs 3d9b3712 extraction): regexg 0.4425 vs 0.4441 s, textproc 1.1222 vs 1.1058 (+1.5 %), subste 0.1793 vs 0.1877, methret 0.0925-0.0967 vs 0.0939 (K=5, noise) -- no change; the match path is not touched.
Guard: Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t last row (differential), inverse-verified on the base extraction.  everyday programs/ref-types -> same (row edited out).
subject: EDGE (pre-existing): a `qr//` object is not BLESSED into `Regexp` for method purposes -- `blessed(qr/x/)` is undef (perl "Regexp") and `qr/x/->isa("Regexp")` DIES "Can't call method isa on unblessed reference" with an SBCL backtrace; `ref(qr/x/)` is "Regexp" and stringification `(?^i:x)` are right
